messages:
alex: quick heads-up — saw a sharp perf cliff on sm86 when SDPA auto-selector flips from v2->v3 around seq_len 512, but only for head_dim 30/46/62. repro attached.

sara: ugh, is this the same as the head_mod/pad mismatch we saw last month?

alex: different. that was kv-cache alignment. this one is selector choosing v3 kernel with higher register pressure => warp divergence. flamegraph attached. kernel mregs spike.

yves: can you paste the probe config and the command you used?

alex: sure:

```bash
./runtime_probe --model gpt-large --head-dim 30 --seq 512 --batch 8 --probe-mode=latency
```

and probe output:

```text
sdpa_v2: 1.9ms
sdpa_v3: 3.8ms  <-- selected
```

sara: interesting it'd be selected despite v3 being slower. selector uses estimated perf from heuristics right? maybe cost model mispredicted due to register spill estimation

yves: I saw that for odd head dims our tile planner rounds up to 64 and triggers a different tiling path. maybe we need a hysteresis so transient probes don't flip in the middle of a workload

alex: proposal: add sequence-length hysteresis window + head-dim bucket smoothing. if current preferred kernel differs only within 10% and the previous kernel has been used recently, keep it. Also add a head_remap path that avoids extra tiling for non-divisible head dims.

sara: makes sense. can we add a quick patch to the autotuner binary and run 24h soak? if it reduces flips we can roll to canary.

alex: I'll open a PR with tests and a trimmed repro. also will attach perf traces and nvprof flamegraphs in the PR.

runtime-bot: deploy check started for alex/headremap-hysteresis (CI: unit+perf)

yves: ping for TL;DR: short-term mitigations?

sara: immediate: pin selector to prefer sdpa_v2 for head_dim % 16 != 0 and seq between 256-1024 until autotuner validated.

alex: will do, and schedule longer term: cost-model retrain and add headdim-aware spill estimator.

sara: awesome. thanks.
